# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 62 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 62 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_062_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Part 8 — Those Who Have Defiled Their Flesh

**62:1** I asked him to explain to me why the flesh is destroyed when the soul is saved. "Listen," he said. "It is because these are the righteous people. They have kept their spirit pure from the beginning and have not defiled it. These are the ones whose spirit the Lord sees and approves, and to whom he gives eternal life."

**62:2** "But those who have kept the commandment of God and have not kept their flesh, and who have defiled it — these too shall live, but the life they shall live will be shorter. As one who knows the commandment of the Lord and does not keep it undertakes his loss himself."

**62:3** "Lord," I said, "I still do not understand. These are the ones who have defiled their flesh — what is this defilement of the flesh?" "Listen," he said. "To go away from God is to defile the flesh. Any man who associates with the deeds of the double-minded goes away from God and defiles himself."

**62:4** "But those who live in forgetfulness and deceive themselves with their knowledge — these too shall live, but not as those who have kept the commandment purely. For those who have departed from God and have sinned and not repented shall die. And those who go away with sorrow are those who have sinned and repented, and on this account they live. But their life is shortened."

**62:5** "When I had heard these things and had understood them well, I said to him: Lord, what do you mean by all these things? And he said to me: I am referring to those who have been called by the name of God, and have wandered through the love of possessions and wealth and power and the vanity of this world. These are the ones who have deprived themselves of God's salvation."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the flesh-defilement theology of Similitude 5.*
